content_voiceover: This table pairs each confirmatory assay with its principle and interpretation, exactly the detail boards like to test. VWF multimer analysis, by two-dimensional immunoelectrophoresis, shows all sizes present in normal, type 1, 2M, and 2N; complete absence in type 3; loss of both large and intermediate multimers in type 2A; and loss of only large multimers in type 2B. Collagen binding, a functional assay of VWF binding to collagen types 1 and 3, is proportionally low relative to antigen in type 1, absent in type 3, and disproportionately low relative to antigen in types 2A and 2B. Ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation tests platelet agglutination across a range of ristocetin doses, and enhanced agglutination at low dose ristocetin is the hallmark of type 2B, though this looks identical to platelet-type VWD, a gain of function GPIb defect, so genetic testing distinguishes the two. Factor eight binding assay measures VWF's capacity to bind factor eight directly, and it's low specifically in type 2N.
keypoints: VWF multimers: absent large+intermediate = 2A; absent large only = 2B
Collagen binding (VWF:CB): disproportionately low vs Ag in 2A/2B
Low-dose RIPA increased in type 2B AND platelet-type VWD (need genetics to differentiate)
VWF:FVIIIB low -> confirms type 2N (defective FVIII binding site)
keypoint_voiceover: Multimer analysis distinguishes 2A, missing large and intermediate multimers, from 2B, missing only large multimers. Collagen binding is disproportionately reduced relative to antigen in both 2A and 2B. Low dose ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation is increased in type 2B, but this looks identical to platelet-type VWD without genetic testing. Factor eight binding assay is the confirmatory test for type 2N.
